news.title: Football: Soccer-For India, World Cup qualification is still just a distant dream
news.lede: July 28 (Reuters) - As the World Cup reached its ⁠final week, Gourav Roy, an Indian software engineer living in San Francisco, drove more than 6,000 miles across the United States to attend both semi-finals and ⁠the final. For Roy, it was the next best thing to what he had grown up dreaming of: seeing India play the World Cup. But the ‌possibility of that dream coming true is looking ever more distant as deep-rooted systemic issues and the failure to implement reforms have left the country of 1.45 billion ranked a lowly 138th in the world, failing to even qualify for next year's Asian Cup. "I've learned to love without expectation.

news.title: Mom Store celebrates the beautiful game of parenthood during World Cup season
news.lede: Mom Store has partnered with independent integrated agency Think Human to launch ‘For the Love of the Beautiful Game’, a social-first campaign that draws parallels between football and parenthood during the World Cup season. Created to capitalise on one of the world’s biggest sporting events while remaining true to the retailer’s parenting focus, the campaign translates familiar football terminology into everyday parenting experiences. At the centre of the campaign is a hero film that uses the energy and language of live football commentary to transform ordinary family moments into match-day highlights.

news.title: Embolo's sending-off in World Cup quarter-final against Argentina was wrong, IFAB says
news.lede: July 28 - Switzerland forward Breel Embolo should not have been sent off during this month's World Cup quarter-final against Argentina, according to a circular issued by soccer's law-making body IFAB on Tuesday. Embolo received a second yellow card during the second half with the match level at 1-1. Argentina struck twice in extra time to beat 10-man Switzerland 3-1 in Kansas City. The 29-year-old had gone down following a challenge by Leandro Paredes, and referee Joao Pinheiro initially booked the Argentina midfielder.

news.title: Neymar's heartbreaking decision after the painful World Cup failure
news.lede: 'The elimination of Brazil from the World Cup shook the foundations of international football and left one of the most striking images of recent years. The legendary forward Neymar Jr once again found himself caught up in a whirlwind of uncertainty over whether he will continue enjoying pulling on his kit or hang up his boots forever.' According to the information revealed by the sports outlet Bitbol and signed by journalist Ezequiel Gasca, the forward is going through the most difficult crossroads of his career after leaving the international tournament in tears. The accumulated frustration after not being able to make the impact he wanted accelerated rumors of an abrupt ending.

news.title: Soccer rules panel clarifies VAR process that World Cup red card for Switzerland's Embolo was wrong
news.lede: Football’s law-making panel clarified its guidance to referees which confirmed Switzerland forward Breel Embolo should not have been sent off in the World Cup quarter-finals against Argentina. Embolo's second yellow card, after a video review for simulating being fouled, changed the momentum of the game in the 72nd minute soon after Switzerland tied the score at 1-1. Argentina won 3-1 in extra time with help from the red-card decision that fuelled complaints, including from previous opponent Egypt, referees were favouring Lionel Messi's team with decisions. The FIFA-backed rules panel known as IFAB published a clarification on Monday (July 27, 2026) that VAR protocol for "mistaken identity" cases was not eligible for that type of incident at the World Cup, though it could be in future competitions.
